$comment: USD per million tokens (`05` §3.9.2). Every Anthropic row was read off platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing on 2026-11-12, and one correction came out of it: Sonnet 5.5's cache read is $0.10, not the $0.20 the plan's table carried — cache hits on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 are 0.05x base input, and 0.05 × $2 is $0.10. A doubled cache-read price would have overstated the cost of the route a family uses most, in the direction that makes the budget guard degrade a group that had not spent its budget. `null` means unknown, and the guard falls back to Opus rates so the error is in the safe direction. OpenAI rows added at `M2-T11`, read off developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing on 2026-11-13. The 30-minute and 12-hour cache-write prices map onto the `cacheWrite5m` and `cacheWrite1h` columns by **slot**, not by equal duration: the columns are the short and long priced slots, and 30m/12h are this provider's. `05` §3.5.4's cost formula predates these columns existing on OpenAI at all and would have charged cache writes at zero. Google rows added at `M2-T13`, read off aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing on 2026-11-13. Four of them carry **promotional** rates with published end dates — `gemini-4-argon` through 2026-11-30 and the two 3.x flash models through 2026-12-31 — so `prices.2026-12-01.json` and `prices.2027-01-01.json` ship beside this file with the standard rates, and `pickTable` moves to each on the day. That is the mechanism `05` §3.9.2 describes, used rather than a reminder nobody would act on: a table that kept a lapsed promotional rate would under-report spend, which is the direction that lets a group overspend its budget without the guard noticing. Gemini has **no billed cache-write category** (caching is implicit), so both write columns are zero rather than absent — a fact about the provider, not a gap.
